title: Ship evidence
description: What `super-ship` records about one ship of one head: the pull-request payload, the pre-flight record and, in `publish`, the ship record of each remote effect with its idempotency key and read-backs. It is evidence about the ship, not the verdict on the change: the receipts and the review verdict it rests on are referenced, never restated. The sensitive actions this run declined are `decision` artifacts and the lesson candidate is a `lesson` draft; neither lives here. Written as a run artifact and never to a repository path (ruling `central-kb-owns-project-artifacts`, docs/decisions/0001-kb-document-vocabulary.md §3).

status.description: The skill's stop condition. There is no cap-reached: remote effects are bounded by the idempotency key, not by counting attempts.

mode.description: 'dry-run' and 'publish' follow the same steps up to the first remote call; 'dry-run' stops there and makes none.

payload.description: The pull-request payload. In 'dry-run' the record holds this payload and the pre-flight record, and no remote effect; the report says what would have been sent and to where.

branch.description: The branch the pull request is, or would be, opened from.

receipts.description: The verification receipts bound to the shipped head that the payload rests on.

review.description: The review verdict bound to the shipped head's artifact hash.

preflight.description: The sensitive-data scan, the dependency-audit triage and each of the project's own release checks, each with its outcome against this head. A check that did not run is recorded as not run, with the reason.

name.description: The project release check's own name, as discovered from the project.

effects.description: The ship record: each remote effect performed, the idempotency key it carried and the read-back result before and after. The key derives from the run id, the operation id, the target identity and the input artifact hash, so a resumed direct publication returns the existing branch or pull request rather than creating a second (adapters/runner-contract/CONTRACT.md §5). Under no-mistakes delivery, super-ship ends at a committed handoff and performs no remote effect (ruling `no-mistakes-as-ship-transport`). No merge is among them.

grant_record.description: Under a Firstmate binding, the record `ak firstmate grant` printed when it granted `ship.prepare` (ADR-0004).

reason.description: What the run needs, or why it failed: the missing or mis-bound input, the unnamed mode, the uncovered sensitive action, the candidate secret, the failed release check or the unknown pull-request lookup.

allOf.description: The envelope's source_revision is the head being shipped, and the receipts and the review verdict must bind to it. Only a run that stopped with needs-input, which is where an unnamed head ends, may leave it null.
A dry run makes no remote call. Not a reduced one, not a single harmless one: none.
A complete ship has emitted the payload and a pre-flight record that holds the sensitive-data scan and the dependency-audit triage.
A complete publish has the branch and the pull request, each with its read-backs recorded.
A run that stops short names what it needs or why it failed.
